sources_considered.why: Primary account distinguishes abundant cloud resources from device-level constraints.
AlexaTM demonstrates large-model research capability but does not identify the principal barrier to a conversational Alexa product.
Describes research directions without ranking the causes of the product limitation.
Full-text retrospective reporting includes employee accounts and Amazon's response. Its later resource constraints are context, not proof about November 2022.

evidence_items.locator: Introduction, paragraph discussing cloud and device resources
evidence_items.explanation: This supports Marcus's premise about substantial cloud capacity in the speech-processing setting. The same account describes difficult device and latency constraints, and does not establish what principally prevented open-ended conversation.

evidence_items.locator: A lack of data made it tough to 'get some magic' out of the LLM
evidence_items.explanation: Employee reporting challenges the assumption that Amazon's resources necessarily satisfied Alexa's needs; Amazon disputed parts of the account. This passage concerns development after the September 2023 demonstration, so it cannot settle the November 2022 causal claim.

unresolved_gaps: No sufficiently specific record establishes the principal constraint on conversational Alexa development by 2022-11-22.
Public descriptions do not show whether available compute and suitable conversational data met the requirements of the intended product.
